grammar: <scheme>-<56 lowercase hex>, whole token <= 96 bytes of [a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*
note: This file is the CONTRACT between the two, vendored byte-identically in python-gen-worker (tests/testdata/) and fenced by scripts/grammar-vector-drift.sh. th#1897 exists because there was no such file: both implementations were internally consistent, they disagreed about `cg-key-v1`, and nothing in either CI could see it — the first mint on the new scheme would have compiled for 45+ minutes and been refused at publish. A change to either implementation that is not a change to this file is the same defect again.

vectors.note: DESIGN-RULINGS 1.38's scheme. Hyphenated and digit-free, which is exactly what the pre-th#1897 `ck<1-2 digits>-` shape could not parse; 66 chars, which is what the pre-th#1897 64-char fragment cap could not hold.
A FUTURE scheme this hub has never seen. th#1183: the hub refuses shape, never scheme, so a newer fleet's key is admitted and ruled on by axes.
The scheme the 3 purged micro-diffusion rows carried.
Two scheme digits — the widest the old shape allowed.
pgw#1176's interim scheme; never minted a real artifact.
One-character scheme. Nothing forbids it.
'.' and '_' are fragment-charset bytes, so a scheme may carry them.

A scheme containing a 20-hex run and three hyphens. THE REGRESSION VECTOR for splitting on '-': the digest is the SUFFIX and the scheme is whatever precedes it, so neither side may split, partition or scan for the first '-'.
Exactly refgrammar.MaxFragmentLen (96) — the boundary, accepted.
empty
A bare digest carries no scheme.
Empty scheme.
55 hex — one short.
57 hex — one long, and it is the tail that is read.
'_' is not the separator; the separator is '-'.
'g' is not hex.
Uppercase hex. The digest is lowercase, byte-wise.
Uppercase scheme; the fragment charset is lowercase.
A space is not in the fragment charset.
'/' is a ref-grammar separator and can never be inside a fragment.
A fragment may not START with '-'.
A trailing byte after the digest — the digest is the suffix.
'#' is a ref-grammar separator.
One past refgrammar.MaxFragmentLen (97) — the boundary, refused.
A cell REF is not a key; KeyRef composes them, KeyFromRef splits them.
The manifest digest is deliberately NOT a key (DESIGN-RULINGS 1.38: 'refused by is_key so nothing can resolve, download, verify or arm it').
